exact_contract_and_proof_review.profile: MellinConvergent f (sigma : Complex) is integrability on x>0 of x^(sigma-1) smul f(x). The helper uses the bijection x=exp(-u), its absolute derivative exp(-u), and complex-power cancellation to prove Integrable (u -> exp(-sigma*u) smul f(exp(-u))).
reverse_hypotheses: sigma is real, F : Complex -> Complex, f : Real -> Complex.
The actual scaled line A(y)=F(sigma+2*pi*y*I) is Integrable over real volume.
For every real x>0, f(x)=mellinInv sigma F x.
exact_contract_and_proof_review.conclusion: For every real y, mellin f (sigma+2*pi*y*I)=F(sigma+2*pi*y*I).
exact_contract_and_proof_review.normalization: Mathlib mellin_eq_fourier evaluates the Fourier transform of exp(-sigma*u) smul f(exp(-u)) at s.im/(2*pi). mellinInv_eq_fourierInv evaluates inverse Fourier at -log x and multiplies by x^(-sigma). Consequently the reverse target is exactly sigma+2*pi*y*I; sign and 2*pi factors are not optional.
exact_contract_and_proof_review.proof: The representation premise identifies the integrable log profile g with inverse Fourier of A. Its reflected argument provides Fourier(A) integrability. Integrable.fourier_fourierInv_eq then applies to A using its actual continuousAt premise. No continuity is inferred from integrability alone.
exact_contract_and_proof_review.no_removed_premise: All upstream hypotheses and proof bodies are retained. The generic theorem does not derive inverse representation, Mellin convergence, spectral line integrability, analytic continuation or arithmetic hypotheses from names or formulas.
